conceptual assets.information: The read/write direction determines whether the cache acknowledges a read, updates a cached word, or issues a backing-bus transfer. Cache behavior depends on this direction to preserve the requested operation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because host_req_i.rw selects read acknowledgement versus write and refill behavior at lines 190-203 and is forwarded or forced onto bus_req_o.rw at lines 159 and 228-239.

conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because host_req_i.ben drives cache_o.we at line 194 and the memory writes selected bytes at lines 413-423, so changing it modifies unintended bytes.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker changes the byte enables so a write corrupts bytes that were not intended to change.

conceptual assets.information: This decision selects direct backing-bus handling instead of the normal cache path for uncached addresses, atomic accesses, or debug accesses. It is generated internally from request attributes and has no separate boundary carrying the decision itself.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because address-region, AMO, and debug tests set ctrl.buf_dir at lines 171-175 and use it to select direct handling at lines 186-203; availability is at risk because forcing the direct path can replace a cache hit with a backing-bus wait at lines 186-203; undermined expected behavior is at risk because the debug/bypass behavior explicitly changes the normal cache path at lines 171-172 and 186-203.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker asserts or induces the debug, atomic, or uncached condition to bypass the cache and obtain incorrect behavior or stall on the backing bus.

conceptual assets.information: The hit decision determines whether a cached value is returned or a line is fetched from the backing bus. It is generated by the cache lookup and has no direct entry or exit port, but it affects observable response timing and bus activity.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the hit decision can be inferred from the different acknowledgement and refill timing at lines 189-203; integrity is at risk because valid and tag state determines hit_o at line 405 and a corrupted result selects the wrong data path; availability is at risk because a forced miss enters a refill that waits for acknowledgements at lines 198-203 and 243-248.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker alters cache lookup state or observes response timing to infer cache residency or force incorrect hits and misses.

conceptual assets.information: The fill operation fetches a missing cache line word by word and writes it into the cache before the original access completes. The cache depends on this internal operation to service misses correctly and eventually release the request.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the fill control generates the refill address, write enable, and new-line command at lines 225-238 and accepts each bus response at lines 242-248; availability is at risk because the cache remains in the refill sequence until bus acknowledgements arrive at lines 243-248, delaying the host response.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker changes refill control or its completion handling so the cache stores a wrong line or remains waiting for a refill indefinitely.

conceptual assets.information: A fence request and its pending state cause the cache to perform its clear and external fence operation before continuing. The cache depends on this control to enforce the requested maintenance and ordering behavior.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the pending fence selects the clear operation at lines 168-170 and 216-220, which clears cache validity through line 381 and emits bus_req_o.fence at line 217; availability is at risk because repeated or stuck fence handling repeatedly diverts the controller into S_CLEAR at lines 168-175 and withholds normal servicing.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker suppresses or repeatedly asserts the fence request so stale cache state is used or normal requests are continually delayed by clearing.

conceptual assets.information: The accumulated refill error records whether a backing-bus response failed and is returned to the host while also controlling refill recovery. Cache operation depends on it to report failures and avoid accepting an erroneous line.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_rsp_i.err is accumulated into ctrl.buf_err at line 242 and controls invalidation and the reported error at lines 254-258, so altering it can hide or invent a refill failure; availability is at risk because a set error produces an error response and aborts the refill at lines 254-258.

conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because ctrl.buf_err causes cache_o.cmd_inv at lines 254-255 and the memory invalidates the selected line at lines 382-383, so suppressing recovery can leave bad data valid; availability is at risk because forced invalidation causes additional misses and refills through lines 255 and 198-203.
